issues.problem: The GUI slot is a NeoForge `SlotItemHandler` wrapped around handlers that do not implement `IItemHandlerModifiable`. When you drop a stack into the slot, `SlotItemHandler.set` casts the handler to `IItemHandlerModifiable` and throws a ClassCastException. That happens on click, on shift-click into an empty slot, and on `quickMoveStack` from slot 0 (`slot.set(EMPTY)`). The storage handler's `getStackInSlot` also returns a copy. `moveItemStackTo` grows that copy instead of the stored amount, so items the player shift-clicks into a partly filled container disappear. Shift-clicking out of the container moves items from the copy without lowering `amount`, so items are duplicated or the game crashes.
issues.reason: The criterion says inserting into the container must not lose items, and the void container must discard what the player inserts. Through the GUI, both containers crash, lose items or duplicate them.
issues.fix: Use a dedicated Slot subclass for the storage and void slots. It should send all changes through the handler: `insertItem` in `safeInsert`/`set`, and `extractItem` in `remove`. Alternatively, give the storage and void containers no item slot and handle insertion and extraction in `quickMoveStack` and `clicked` through `insertItem`/`extractItem`. Either way the stored `amount` must be the only source of truth.

history.note: fixed: GUI slots now insert and extract through the handlers, keeping the stored amount authoritative.

ContainerInputSlot sends set, remove and safeInsert through the handler's insertItem and extractItem. The menus' quickMoveStack insert and extract through the handler too, so the stored amount stays authoritative.

issues.problem: `craftOne` calls `planCraft` once per craft, and every call runs `RecipeManager.getRecipeFor(RecipeType.CRAFTING, ...)` with no last-recipe hint. A Tier 9 machine runs up to 256 full crafting-recipe searches every tick, Tier 8 runs 64, and Tier 7 runs 16.
issues.reason: Every search walks all loaded crafting recipes. With the original cycles of 1 tick and up to 256 crafts per cycle, one machine can cost hundreds of thousands of recipe matches per tick. Vanilla's crafter and the crafting menu avoid this by reusing the last matched recipe.
issues.fix: Find the recipe once per cycle, or cache the last `RecipeHolder<CraftingRecipe>` and pass it to `getRecipeFor(type, input, level, lastRecipe)`. Recheck `matches` against the actual `CraftingInput` before each commit, so data-component differences are still validated.

history.note: fixed: 周期内で直前の RecipeHolder を検索ヒントとして再利用し、各製作前に実際の CraftingInput との一致を再確認します。
The last RecipeHolder is passed as a hint to getRecipeFor within a cycle, and matches() is rechecked against the actual input before each craft.

issues.problem: The result preview is recomputed only when the pattern changes or the block entity loads (`previewDirty`). After `/reload` or any datapack change, the preview keeps the old result even though crafting now uses the new RecipeManager.
issues.reason: The criterion requires an accurate result display. AGENTS.md M03 says recipe reloads notify machines and displays through `ClayiumRecipesReloadedEvent`, as `ClayMachineBlockEntity` does. This block entity does not subscribe, so a removed or changed recipe still shows the old output.
issues.fix: Set `previewDirty = true` when `ClayiumRecipesReloadedEvent` fires, using the same listener pattern as `ClayMachineBlockEntity`. Alternatively, recompute the preview from the per-cycle recipe lookup, so the shown result always matches the recipe used for crafting.

history.note: fixed: ClayiumRecipesReloadedEvent で結果プレビューを再計算対象にしました。
A ClayiumRecipesReloadedEvent listener sets previewDirty on loaded crafters whose level uses the reloaded RecipeManager. The event exposes recipeManager().

issues.problem: `tickServer` calls `setChangedAndSync()` at the end of every cycle, even when nothing was crafted. For Tier 6 to 9 that is every tick. Each call runs `sendBlockUpdated`, which sends the full `saveWithoutMetadata` tag (16-slot inventory, pattern and energy) to every tracking client. The non-cycle ticks also call `setChanged()` with no state change except `craftTick`.
issues.reason: No client-side renderer reads this block entity's data. The menu already syncs slots and `ContainerData`. Sending block updates every tick for idle machines wastes network bandwidth and triggers neighbour/render updates for no use.
issues.fix: Call `setChanged()` (and a sync only if a client consumer actually needs it) only when a craft committed or stored state changed. Remove `getUpdateTag`/`getUpdatePacket` and the `sendBlockUpdated` path unless a client feature reads the block entity data.

history.note: fixed: 毎周期のブロック更新送信と未使用の更新パケットを削除し、保存状態が変わったときだけ setChanged を呼びます。
setChangedAndSync, getUpdateTag and getUpdatePacket are gone. Only setChanged remains, and it is skipped on every-tick cycles where nothing was crafted.
